dispositions.exploration_candidate: a target listed for a need whose direction is unresolved (or an action with no stated sign): exploration only
dispositions.incomplete_or_failed_query: an ABSENCE conclusion (no link or no target row) that depends on a mechanism or identity source in a FAILED, INCOMPLETE or NOT_FETCHED state: NOT a negative. Positive evidence from a working source is not changed by it, and an accessibility-source error never produces it (a stale source adds a caveat instead)
dispositions.insufficient_data: a link or an intervention exists but the sign, the identity or the observation needed to decide is missing
dispositions.mixed_consistent_and_opposed_actions: the same family has BOTH a direction-consistent and an opposed action on this need; both are listed with target, action and source and no sign is summed: not a favourable profile
dispositions.no_catalogue_link_found: identity resolved and targets catalogued, none an intervention target of this need (a statement about the catalogue and its possibly stale sources, not about relevance)
dispositions.opposite_mechanism: the stated action opposes the need's direction (and no consistent action is catalogued)
dispositions.source_queried_without_result: the sources were queried and returned no target or mechanism row for this record

no_probability: nothing here is a probability of benefit or cure

card_endpoint_pursued: Step 0 (gate): in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic corrected human neural cultures that contain microglia or CNS-macrophage-like cells (and, as a second system, Wwox-null mouse primary neuron-glia co-culture): nuclear NRF2 and KEAP1 protein, NQO1 enzyme activity and the transcripts NQO1, HMOX1, GCLM, SRXN1, ROS (roGFP/CellROX/MitoSOX) at baseline and after an oxidative challenge, and IL-6 and IL-1beta PROTEIN (and caspase-1 p20 if an inflammasome readout is used) after LPS (with and without ATP). Step 1: NFE2L2-dependence-controlled activation (KEAP1 knockdown; omaveloxolone; dimethyl fumarate and monomethyl fumarate as separate arms, never one row) with NFE2L2 knockdown or loss as the dependence control for every compound, in both genotypes, reading viability, lipid peroxidation, network activity (MEA), SOX2/NEUN fractions, and cytokine protein. Off-NRF2 readouts for the fumarates: NF-kB p65 nuclear translocation, HCAR2 dependence (HCAR2 knockdown or an antagonist) and GAPDH activity. Omaveloxolone is read over a concentration series that spans the low-nM NRF2-linked window and the hundreds-of-nM window in which IKK/NF-kB, JNK and growth effects were reported, reading NQO1 at each point (in-vitro facts of the source, not a dose recommendation), with free (unbound) exposure reported where serum is present. The system for step 0 also includes an astrocyte-containing challenged arm (LPS with and without ATP) and records the clone and batch of every sample, keeping both clones. Decided by: ROS, viability, network activity and cytokine protein. Not decided by: GFAP/IBA1 counts (held-out endpoints) or the six IT7 readout genes (guard IT7_READOUT6).

card_endpoint_pursued: In WWOX-deficient versus corrected (isogenic add-back) human neural cells, at 5 percent oxygen (physioxia) as the primary condition beside 21 and 1 percent: HIF-1alpha and HIF-2alpha protein, nuclear and cytoplasmic, then whether lowering the axis (genetic HIF1A and EPAS1 knockdown, singly and together; a PX-478-class lever as a second arm) lowers lactate or extracellular acidification, glucose uptake and the five other members of the guard-scope 10-gene glycolysis set reported individually (a change there confirms the seed, it does not validate a lever), and what that does to network activity (multielectrode array), viability and SOX2/NEUN fractions. The direction of the HIF change is not established (two-sided literature, all non-WWOX): raising HIF is a conditional arm (H-protect), lowering it a conditional arm (H-harm), and three rivals that need no HIF role (culture state or composition, neuronal activity, MYC) have their own arms. The deciding readout is lactate or extracellular acidification and glucose uptake plus the five genes PGK1, ALDOA, ENO1, PFKP and PKM reported individually; the six IT7 readout genes and the 10-gene glycolysis set they belong to are guard-scope members and cannot decide.

card_endpoint_pursued: In WWOX-deficient versus corrected (isogenic add-back) human neural cells, at 5 percent oxygen (physioxia) as the primary condition beside 21 and 1 percent: HIF-1alpha and HIF-2alpha protein, nuclear and cytoplasmic, then whether lowering the axis (genetic HIF1A and EPAS1 knockdown, singly and together; a PX-478-class lever as a second arm) lowers lactate or extracellular acidification, glucose uptake and the five other members of the guard-scope 10-gene glycolysis set reported individually (a change there confirms the seed, it does not validate a lever), and what that does to network activity (multielectrode array), viability and SOX2/NEUN fractions. The direction of the HIF change is not established (two-sided literature, all non-WWOX): raising HIF is a conditional arm (H-protect), lowering it a conditional arm (H-harm), and three rivals that need no HIF role (culture state or composition, neuronal activity, MYC) have their own arms. The deciding readout is lactate or extracellular acidification and glucose uptake plus the five genes PGK1, ALDOA, ENO1, PFKP and PKM reported individually; the six IT7 readout genes and the 10-gene glycolysis set they belong to are guard-scope members and cannot decide.

card_endpoint_pursued: Step 0 (gate): in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic corrected human neural cultures that contain microglia or CNS-macrophage-like cells (and, as a second system, Wwox-null mouse primary neuron-glia co-culture): nuclear NRF2 and KEAP1 protein, NQO1 enzyme activity and the transcripts NQO1, HMOX1, GCLM, SRXN1, ROS (roGFP/CellROX/MitoSOX) at baseline and after an oxidative challenge, and IL-6 and IL-1beta PROTEIN (and caspase-1 p20 if an inflammasome readout is used) after LPS (with and without ATP). Step 1: NFE2L2-dependence-controlled activation (KEAP1 knockdown; omaveloxolone; dimethyl fumarate and monomethyl fumarate as separate arms, never one row) with NFE2L2 knockdown or loss as the dependence control for every compound, in both genotypes, reading viability, lipid peroxidation, network activity (MEA), SOX2/NEUN fractions, and cytokine protein. Off-NRF2 readouts for the fumarates: NF-kB p65 nuclear translocation, HCAR2 dependence (HCAR2 knockdown or an antagonist) and GAPDH activity. Omaveloxolone is read over a concentration series that spans the low-nM NRF2-linked window and the hundreds-of-nM window in which IKK/NF-kB, JNK and growth effects were reported, reading NQO1 at each point (in-vitro facts of the source, not a dose recommendation), with free (unbound) exposure reported where serum is present. The system for step 0 also includes an astrocyte-containing challenged arm (LPS with and without ATP) and records the clone and batch of every sample, keeping both clones. Decided by: ROS, viability, network activity and cytokine protein. Not decided by: GFAP/IBA1 counts (held-out endpoints) or the six IT7 readout genes (guard IT7_READOUT6).

card_endpoint_pursued: Step 0 (gate): in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic corrected human neural cultures that contain microglia or CNS-macrophage-like cells (and, as a second system, Wwox-null mouse primary neuron-glia co-culture): nuclear NRF2 and KEAP1 protein, NQO1 enzyme activity and the transcripts NQO1, HMOX1, GCLM, SRXN1, ROS (roGFP/CellROX/MitoSOX) at baseline and after an oxidative challenge, and IL-6 and IL-1beta PROTEIN (and caspase-1 p20 if an inflammasome readout is used) after LPS (with and without ATP). Step 1: NFE2L2-dependence-controlled activation (KEAP1 knockdown; omaveloxolone; dimethyl fumarate and monomethyl fumarate as separate arms, never one row) with NFE2L2 knockdown or loss as the dependence control for every compound, in both genotypes, reading viability, lipid peroxidation, network activity (MEA), SOX2/NEUN fractions, and cytokine protein. Off-NRF2 readouts for the fumarates: NF-kB p65 nuclear translocation, HCAR2 dependence (HCAR2 knockdown or an antagonist) and GAPDH activity. Omaveloxolone is read over a concentration series that spans the low-nM NRF2-linked window and the hundreds-of-nM window in which IKK/NF-kB, JNK and growth effects were reported, reading NQO1 at each point (in-vitro facts of the source, not a dose recommendation), with free (unbound) exposure reported where serum is present. The system for step 0 also includes an astrocyte-containing challenged arm (LPS with and without ATP) and records the clone and batch of every sample, keeping both clones. Decided by: ROS, viability, network activity and cytokine protein. Not decided by: GFAP/IBA1 counts (held-out endpoints) or the six IT7 readout genes (guard IT7_READOUT6).

card_endpoint_pursued: Step 0 (gate): in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic corrected human neural cultures that contain microglia or CNS-macrophage-like cells (and, as a second system, Wwox-null mouse primary neuron-glia co-culture): nuclear NRF2 and KEAP1 protein, NQO1 enzyme activity and the transcripts NQO1, HMOX1, GCLM, SRXN1, ROS (roGFP/CellROX/MitoSOX) at baseline and after an oxidative challenge, and IL-6 and IL-1beta PROTEIN (and caspase-1 p20 if an inflammasome readout is used) after LPS (with and without ATP). Step 1: NFE2L2-dependence-controlled activation (KEAP1 knockdown; omaveloxolone; dimethyl fumarate and monomethyl fumarate as separate arms, never one row) with NFE2L2 knockdown or loss as the dependence control for every compound, in both genotypes, reading viability, lipid peroxidation, network activity (MEA), SOX2/NEUN fractions, and cytokine protein. Off-NRF2 readouts for the fumarates: NF-kB p65 nuclear translocation, HCAR2 dependence (HCAR2 knockdown or an antagonist) and GAPDH activity. Omaveloxolone is read over a concentration series that spans the low-nM NRF2-linked window and the hundreds-of-nM window in which IKK/NF-kB, JNK and growth effects were reported, reading NQO1 at each point (in-vitro facts of the source, not a dose recommendation), with free (unbound) exposure reported where serum is present. The system for step 0 also includes an astrocyte-containing challenged arm (LPS with and without ATP) and records the clone and batch of every sample, keeping both clones. Decided by: ROS, viability, network activity and cytokine protein. Not decided by: GFAP/IBA1 counts (held-out endpoints) or the six IT7 readout genes (guard IT7_READOUT6).
